moat_against: No recurring revenue, consumables lock-in or switching costs
Hit-driven growth; core US categories grow only mid-to-high single digits
Intense competition (Dyson, iRobot, Breville, Keurig, private label) and constant patent litigation
Retailer/shelf-space concentration — distribution is rented, not owned
Tariff exposure across Southeast Asia supply; expected ~$247.1M refund is one-off
Controlling shareholder (JS Global ties) and product-recall risk (Foodi recall, 2025)
moat_for: Leading Shark/Ninja brand share in many US small-appliance and floorcare categories
Proven category-creation engine, ~25 launches/yr (CREAMi, SLUSHi, Luxe Café, CryoGlow)
Social-first + omnichannel distribution flywheel (retail, Amazon, DTC, TikTok Shop)
Supply-chain agility: ~90-100% of US volume moved out of China ahead of rivals
Premium-but-accessible pricing with ~48.7% adjusted gross margin under tariff pressure
moat_justification: Two strong consumer brands (Shark, Ninja) with leading share in many small-appliance categories and a repeatable category-creation/marketing engine (~25 launches/yr), plus a supply-chain lead from moving ~90-100% of US volume out of China. But no recurring revenue, lock-in or switching costs — every purchase is a fresh contest, growth is hit-driven, distribution is rented from retailers, and pricing sits deliberately below premium rivals, capping pricing power. Moderate/narrow moat: 5/10, CAP 8.5 years.
name: SharkNinja, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality hit-driven appliance brands, moat 5/10 — at $186.32 even the super-bull case returns only 12.9%; weighted IRR 8.3% (Tier D), clears 15% only at or below $79.13.
